_doc: Street centreline paths and the visible travelled strips for the 1 July 1835 scene. The platted corridors are 80 ft (24.384 m) wide; the bare or thinly grassed track drawn inside one is narrower and explicitly conjectural. Paths are analytic extensions of the committed street-control module and the 1834 plats, not traces of modern pavement. A path is clipped wherever the heightfield is water, so a platted line never paints an invented ford across a branch of the river. Surface classes follow chicago_dpw_1891_streets: earth only on this date. South Water and Lake are the early principal graded/turnpiked routes; the fall-1836 work on Canal, western Lake, and Randolph is not backdated. The Gurdon Hubbard La Salle segment is omitted as a special improvement because his petition is dated twelve days after this scene. `path_local_enu_m` is the PLATTED line and it is what the plat, corridor and lot derivations read; a street may also carry `drawn_track_local_enu_m`, which is the worn wheel line the renderer paints and which those derivations ignore. The two are separate claims and one field cannot carry both — a bend added to the plat line moves platted lot lines the whole length of the street and re-scores the corridor-intrusion count (measured on T-0111, both gates red). A drawn track is checked at compile time to stay inside its own platted corridor and to overhang the platted line's ends by no more than 4 m, so it can meet a bridge abutment and cannot become an unplatted street.
surface_standard: No gravel or hard paving is shown. 'graded' and 'turnpiked' are rendered as drained or thrown-up earth with wagon wear; ordinary streets are worn native soil with a grassy crown and margins.

west_end.basis: the 1834 sheets and the committed bank
west_end.derivation: Market Street's platted centreline, which is the line through the data box at N -400 and the committed control point `lake_market`, carried NORTH until the committed heightfield e1834_harbor_cut turns wet. The last dry sample on that line is local (89.51, -71.02), bisected to 0.01 m against the same water test tools/generate_plat_lots.py uses (a sample is wet where the field does not cover it or covers it below the datum surface). South Water's west end is closed there and one vertex, (101, -71), carries the line east along the point of land to the committed (120, -57) without crossing water: every 0.5 m sample of both new segments is dry. The old west end (100, -101) ran 30 m DOWN the South Branch's east bank past Lake Street's own latitude, which is Market Street's ground and not this street's, and it is what made blk_south_water_market impossible to build.
west_end.not_control: THIS END IS NOT DERIVED CONTROL AND IS NOT GRADED AS THOUGH IT WERE. `node_rule` refuses this corner and the refusal stands: Market's and South Water's modern successors — North Upper Wacker Drive and West Upper Wacker Drive — are one carriageway pair changing name through a BEND at the Lake Street junction, so the only nodes they share are `lake_market`'s own two, 110 m south of the corner they would name (measured 2026-08-27, `refused_control.market_south_water` in data/traces/street_control.json). `python3 tools/refetch_control.py --discover market_south_water` still exits 1, and softening that refusal to make this end pass would be the wrong repair.
west_end.authorised_by: The owner's ruling of 2026-08-29 on ticket T-0183, taken after the refusal was measured: close the west end on Market's corridor from the 1834 sheets and the committed bank — the same basis the rest of this curve already stands on — and grade it for what it is.

streets.note: The curved west approach follows the dry south bank resolved by the committed heightfield; east of Franklin the line follows the modern Wacker control used by the structure placements but is shifted into the dry half of the platted riverfront corridor, AND SINCE 2026-08-28 THAT SHIFT IS A MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN A SENTENCE: 8.28 m south, measured perpendicular to this centreline from `control.south_water_franklin` in data/traces/street_control.json, the first control point ever committed on this street. That is 68 per cent of the 12.192 m half of the 80 ft platted module, so the line sits inside the corridor's dry half with 3.91 m to spare before its south edge if the corridor is centred on the modern junction. Nothing was re-derived and nothing moved — the standoff is the reconstruction decision this note already described, and it is now checkable. The corner of the two committed centrelines falls at local (208.49, +2.83) against the control's (208.46, +11.41): the whole 8.58 m disagreement is across this street and 0.03 m of it is across Franklin. The street stops at the United States Reservation, matching the 1833 order. Track width and ruts are visual interpretation, not measurements. THE WEST END WAS CLOSED ON MARKET'S CORRIDOR ON 2026-08-30 (T-0183): the line used to stop at (100, -101), 30 m down the South Branch's east bank and 24 m short of Market's east block edge, and it now ends at the corner (89.51, -71.02) where Market's platted centreline meets the committed 1834 bank. See `west_end` above for the derivation and for the grade — that corner has NO derivable control and does not pretend to. blk_south_water_market builds because of it.

The two verified Lake intersections fix the line. The official chronology calls Lake one of the two principal early turnpiked and graded streets, but separately dates its western extension to Desplaines to fall 1836; the 1835 visual treatment therefore stays earth and does not imply that every western block had already received the later work.
The fall-1836 turnpiking recorded for Randolph is deliberately not backdated.

north_end.note: Market's committed centreline used to stop at `lake_market`, its only control point, where Lake Street crosses it. It is carried the further ~39 m north to the committed 1834 bank so that South Water Street's west end has a corridor to close on; the added vertex is collinear with the control the line already stood on, so nothing between Lake and the data box moved. North of `lake_market` this line is an extension and not control — see `south_water.west_end` and liberty L214.

streets.note: The north end of this line is the one place on the reconstruction where a modern junction can be made on South Water Street, and 2026-08-28 it was: `control.south_water_franklin` in data/traces/street_control.json, the mean of Franklin's two crossings of Wacker Drive's carriageways. The committed line extended to that junction's northing gives easting 208.49 against the control's 208.46 — 0.03 m. That is a reproduction, not an independent confirmation: `osm_streets_2026` is already one of this record's sources, so what it establishes is that the line can be re-derived from the source it names, which until now it could not be. Nothing moved.

Hubbard's petition says he had graded and thrown up the short South Water-to-Lake segment, but is dated 13 July 1835. On the scene date twelve days earlier this path therefore receives no special improved treatment.

streets.drawn_track_note: The platted line stops at [699, 18], on the crest of the drawbridge approach fill, 2.70 m short of the causeway. The worn wheel line does not: it leaves the platted line at the South Water corner and runs one straight 13.8 m chord onto the fill's own axis, ending on the deck. RECONSTRUCTED, and what bounds it is measured. The last point IS the deck end — the south edge midpoint of the dearborn_street_drawbridge footprint, local E 697.65 / N 20.70, which is also line[0] of the dearborn_south approach in terrain_spec.json, so nothing here invents where the boards begin. The first point is the platted line at N 7.0, which is where south_water crosses it, so the swing starts at the corner the traffic comes from rather than at a chosen station. Held on the platted line the track's east edge would stand 4.87 m off the fill's axis, 0.87 m outside the 4.0 m half-width the earthwork is level across, and the last stride onto the causeway would be taken on a side slope; swung onto the axis, every metre of the 7 m width ends on the level crest. What is invented is that the swing is one chord and takes 13.8 m. ONE chord because the ribbon's panels are drawn square to their own chord and are not mitred at the joints, so each turn opens a wedge of prairie on the outside of it (3.5 tan(turn/2) wide at the ribbon's edge, nothing at its centre) and one 5.7-degree joint is the fewest and smallest a swing can be cut into: a 0.61 m2 sector, 0.17 m at its widest, inside the 0.84 m the road texture's own edge already fades out across — and because the joint stands at the corner, South Water Street's own 10.5 m roadway is drawn over half of it, so 0.30 m2 is what a 2 cm plan probe finds uncovered by any street. An eight-chord easement was measured first and was seven times worse (2.18 m2), because eight joints turn eight times. The line is never more than 1.37 m off the platted line, a ninth of the 80 ft corridor. See docs/LIBERTIES.md L178 and ticket T-0111.

streets.note: The line uses the road-only Kinzie control already adopted by the North Branch bridge rather than the queued five-node bikeway-inclusive GCP. Its recorded turnpiking belongs to fall 1836 and is not backdated.

DERIVED FROM THE COMMITTED NORTH BANK by tools/derive_north_water.py, not drawn beside it. The line this replaced was a hand-drawn schematic that ran 477.4 m of its 843.3 m INSIDE the terrain's water mask, so the renderer drew no roadway at all across that reach and three of its six bends stood in the river (T-0226). The bank is a trace of Wright 1834 with a stated +/-20 m; this line was not a trace of anything and said so; the old line missed the bank by 1 to 86 m, up to 4.3x that uncertainty; and the North Division placement recipe had already ruled that proximity to North Water Street never overrides the water mask. So the street was the record that was wrong. North Water Street fronted the main stem, so its platted corridor is laid with its south line on the bank and the centreline half a platted street clear of it - 12.192 m, half the 80 ft thompson_module_1830. THAT HALF MODULE IS A DISTANCE, so the requirement at each 5 m station is the bank's OFFSET CURVE: the northern boundary of the traced bank dilated by a 12.192 m disc, which is the locus of points exactly half a street from the bank whatever bearing the bank runs at. It is fitted in the fewest straight runs that clear every station with 0.5 m of give, which is 2.5 % of the bank trace's own uncertainty. Until T-0307 the requirement was instead the bank's running maximum over +/-15 m of easting plus a NORTHWARD setback, and both halves of that assume an east-west bank; see WHAT THE WEST REACH COSTS, stated because the tool measures it (T-0307, which re-derived it). Coming round Wolf Point into the forks the bank falls 45 m of northing in 35 m of easting. Under the old rule a running maximum taken 15 m ahead of a bank that steep added most of that drop to the setback, and a northward offset bought only its cosine back, so the road stood up to 41.5 m from the water on the tool's own northward-ray reading - three and a half street widths where a half module is 12.2. The offset curve states the intended thing at any bearing and the verge came in. Measured as nearest water in any direction, which is the honest perpendicular distance and is also new in T-0307: west of the slough 5.50 m .. 25.50 m before, 5.50 m .. 20.00 m after; east of the slough 9.50 m .. 25.50 m before, 8.50 m .. 20.50 m after; the dry climb to Kinzie unmoved at 12.00 m .. 27.00 m. The line went from 19 authored bends to 24, which is the cost of following a bank instead of a lookahead. THE TWO TIGHT SPOTS ARE INHERITED AND UNMOVED. The 5.50 m is the street's own west terminus at [-30, 45.2], a vertex this derivation did not move: the setback rule reads the main stem's north bank at that easting and has nothing to say about the North Branch lying to the WEST of the terminus, and the street ends at the fork because that is where the street ended. The 8.50 m is the slough crossing's east abutment, where the street is anchored on the deck rather than on the setback and the crossing owns the water. Both are filed as T-0372 rather than tuned here. Geometry stays reconstructed - a bank is a proxy for a street, not evidence of one, and west of the slough there is not even a building on it. Track width and wear remain visual interpretation.

THE ROAD THE FORT PLAINLY HAD, DRAWN AT THE RECONSTRUCTED TIER, and which part is which is stated rather than implied. WHAT IS DOCUMENTED: the fort had large gates north and south - Juliette Kinzie inside it in 1831, Andreas independently, and a break in each of those two walls and in neither of the others on the 1830 Harrison plan - and the garrison garden's own record reads off that same plan that the plot lies 'west of the road'. So the plan draws a road on the reservation, and a road that is east of that garden and arrives at that gate has to run about here. WHAT IS NOT DOCUMENTED: nobody traced this line, nobody measured it, and no source names it. The 1835 name is DESCRIPTIVE, not a proper name; the 2026 name is the street that runs over this ground today, not a descent of name. THE WESTERN REACH IS THE INVENTION AND IT IS THE REASON THIS RECORD IS RECONSTRUCTED: South Water Street stops at the United States Reservation, matching the 1833 order, so the connection from the town to the fort gate was never a platted street - it is drawn because a garrisoned post that mustered, traded and drew its stores through the town had a way in, and a visitor who walks east out of South Water Street should find one instead of trackless prairie. The line is routed clear of the garden's east corner and of the Beaubien buildings, and it is clipped by the water mask like every other track, so it makes honest gaps rather than fords where the ground is wet. Recorded in docs/LIBERTIES.md; T-0044.

streets.name_2026: N Michigan Avenue, at the bridge's south approach
streets.note: THE TRACK p4_0 DRAWS DESCENDING THE BANK FROM THE NORTH GATE, held back by L140 until the bank it descends had been graded (T-0004) and built now that it has (T-0099). WHICH PART IS WHICH. WHAT IS DOCUMENTED: the fort's north gate — 'large gates opened to the north and south' (Juliette Kinzie, inside it in 1831), 'one on the north and the other on the south side' (Andreas), a break in each of those two walls and in neither of the others on the 1830 Harrison plan — and that the plan names a ferry among the ground round the fort. WHAT IS NOT DOCUMENTED: this line. Nobody traced it, nobody measured it, and no source names it; the 1835 name is DESCRIPTIVE, and the 2026 name is the ground the modern bridge approach covers, not a descent of name. BOTH ENDS ARE DERIVED FROM COMMITTED RECORDS AND THE MIDDLE IS ONE STRAIGHT CHORD. It begins at [1156.63, 253.92]: the north gate's own centre — 26.5 m along a 53 m wall, the midpoint tools/measure_fort_gates.py reads the shipped leaves at — carried out along the wall's outward normal by 6.74 m, which is the standoff the fort road already keeps from the SOUTH gate. The apron's bare trodden earth carries the last stride to the pickets at both gates, and this record invents no second convention for the north one. It ends at [1133.40, 259.61]: the Z = 0 waterline of the committed heightfield, on the easting of the WEST END of the commandant's quarters — the one place on this bank any source puts anything, the 1855 Hesler key locating the ferry landing 'under the west chimney of the Commandant's quarters'. READ THE DATE: that key is 1855 and describes the post-military compound, so it is read here as an inference that a landing fixed by the shape of a bank stood where it stood twenty years earlier, and never as a measurement of 1835. WHY ONE OBLIQUE CHORD AND NOT A RAMP STRAIGHT DOWN. Straight north out of the gate the graded bank falls 3.60 m in under 10 m, about 1 in 2.7, which is a scramble rather than a way to a boat. Swung west onto the landing the same fall is spread over 23.91 m: 1 in 6.65 mean and 1 in 3.65 at its steepest metre, measured on the committed heightfield at [1140.0, 257.99]. That worst metre is GENTLER THAN GROUND THIS PROJECT ALREADY DRAWS ROADWAY ON — South Water Street reaches 1 in 3.0 at the river bank, Randolph and Washington 1 in 4.1 — so the obliquity is what makes the track walkable and is not a shape chosen for its own sake. One chord means no joint, so no wedge of prairie opens at a bend (L178). The width is the GATE'S: 3.60 m, the committed gate_width_m of the palisade this track leaves by, rather than a fourth invented figure on this reservation. The corridor is the fort road's 12.0 m for the same reason. Clipped by the water mask like every other track, so the ribbon stops at the water instead of painting a ford. Recorded in docs/LIBERTIES.md L199; T-0099.
